eyebrow: Loading to SQLite — a lightweight stand-in for a warehouse
caption: sqlite3 is built into Python — no install, no server. df.to_sql() works the same way it did in Lesson 30's SQLAlchemy engine.

code:
def count_rows(db_path="orders_warehouse.db", table="orders"):
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
    try:
        cursor = conn.cursor()
        cursor.execute(f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {table};")
        return cursor.fetchone()[0]
    finally:
        conn.close()

print(count_rows())
caption: Loading isn't done until you've confirmed the row count in the target matches what you expected to load.

eyebrow: The same pattern, pointed at AdventureWorks2012
code:
from sqlalchemy import create_engine

engine = create_engine(
    "mssql+pyodbc://@localhost/AdventureWorks2012"
    "?driver=ODBC+Driver+18+for+SQL+Server&trusted_connection=yes"
)
df.to_sql("OrdersStaging", engine, schema="Staging", if_exists="append", index=False)
caption: Same to_sql() call, same DataFrame — only the connection changes. The rest of the pipeline doesn't need to care.
